exercise.name: Cable Seated Wide Grip Row
aliases: Seated row with a long bar

reference.title: Cable Seated Wide grip Row
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (proxy refused gymvisual.com), so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (horizontal abduction and extension, scapular retraction, elbow flexion)

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you row the bar to the lower chest, breathe in as the arms reach forward.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s pull, short squeeze, about 2 s return

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Cable stack load is user-chosen: usually a little lighter than a close-grip row.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then one plate on the stack; add a 1 s squeeze

cues.text: Sit tall facing the low pulley, feet braced on the foot plate, knees slightly bent; hold a long bar overhand, hands well outside the shoulders, arms long, chest a little forward.
Breathe out; sit tall and row the bar to the lower chest, elbows travelling back and out at about 45-70 degrees from the sides.
Shoulder blades together, elbows behind the trunk, chest up and shoulders down.
Breathe in and let the arms reach forward under control, shoulder blades sliding forward.
Brief stretch at full reach with a long spine, then row again.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning far back to finish the rep
mistakes.fix: Keep the trunk between slightly forward and upright; lighten the stack.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging as the bar comes in
mistakes.fix: Draw the shoulder blades back and down.
Keep the wrists straight, knuckles in line with the forearms.

mistakes.mistake: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides at shoulder height
mistakes.fix: Let the elbows travel back and out, below shoulder height, to the lower chest.

kinematics.setup: ≈9° forward of upright at the reach
kinematics.norm: From slightly forward at the reach to upright at the finish, neutral spine (Fenwick 2009)
From nearly straight to about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Upper arm ≈78° from the trunk line, reaching forward
kinematics.peak: Upper arm ≈66° from the trunk, elbows 11 cm behind the shoulders and 19 cm out
kinematics.norm: Elbows back and out at about 45-70 degrees from the trunk; with the arm raised, horizontal abduction works the posterior deltoid (Schoenfeld 2013)
Protracted at the reach, retracted at the finish (Oyama 2010)

kinematics.setup: Overhand, 76 cm between the hands on a 120 cm bar (shoulders 40 cm apart)
kinematics.norm: Overhand, about 1.5 times shoulder width (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 1.2 s pull, 0.4 s squeeze, 2 s return
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 1 s pull and 2 s return (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Cable Seated Wide grip Row, video (movement reference)
Lehman et al. 2004, variations in muscle activation levels during traditional latissimus dorsi weight training exercises (Dynamic Medicine 3:4)
Fenwick, Brown & McGill 2009, comparison of different rowing exercises: trunk muscle activation and lumbar spine motion, load and stiffness (J Strength Cond Res 23(2):350-358)
Oyama, Myers, Wassinger and Lephart 2010, three-dimensional scapular and clavicular kinematics and scapular muscle activity during retraction exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 40(3):169-179)
Schoenfeld et al. 2013, effect of hand position on EMG activity of the posterior shoulder musculature during a horizontal abduction exercise (J Strength Cond Res 27(10):2644-2649)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
The cable load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can move with the trunk still and the shoulders down.
At the end of the set, lean forward and let the bar back to the stack slowly.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: bring the hands in a little and the elbows closer to the sides (clinical opinion).
Low-back discomfort: keep the trunk upright with no lean at the reach.

muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Prime mover: draws the shoulder blades together at the finish.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Prime mover: draws the shoulder blades together at the finish.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm back and out with the elbows wide.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Prime mover: pulls the upper arm back and out with the elbows wide.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Helps pull the upper arm back.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Helps pull the upper arm back.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Holds the head of the arm bone centred as the elbows go back.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Holds the head of the arm bone centred as the elbows go back.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the spine long against the cable.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the spine long against the cable.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Steadies the shoulder girdle; should not shrug.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Steadies the shoulder girdle; should not shrug.

guides.label: Bar to the lower chest, elbows wide
